design_dependencies.statement: Boolean result classification in host language model must represent ECMAScript Boolean values and predicates for isBoolean and value comparisons.
Numeric model must expose distinction checks for +0ℱ, -0ℱ, NaN and BigInt zero for falsy branch behavior.
Object representation must expose whether an argument has [[IsHTMLDDA]] slot for web-compat branch.

assumptions.statement: Interpretation assumes a shared ECMAScript value model already defines object typing and String/Number/BigInt/Boolean recognizers used by ToBoolean.
Interpretation assumes that the subscripted notation +0𝔽, -0𝔽, and 0ℤ map to the canonical Number and BigInt constants used by the shared value model.

ambiguities.statement: The ToBoolean clause declares Object with [[IsHTMLDDA]] as falsey but does not enumerate all object kinds that may carry that slot; source states it is host-defined and notes only document.all as known.
Behavior for symbol values is implied by the default true branch, but this inference is indirect and relies on branch completeness.

open_questions.statement: Whether this construct inherits any host/target availability constraints from broader runtime context is not stated in the bounded source.
Whether implementation restrictions for checking [[IsHTMLDDA]] in host objects are constrained beyond the cited web-compat note is not separately bounded by this unit.

semantic_claims.statement: ToBoolean is an abstract operation with name/section 7.1.2 that takes one argument named argument and returns a Boolean.
If argument is a Boolean, ToBoolean returns the same Boolean value.
If argument is one of undefined, null, +0ℱ, -0ℱ, NaN, 0ℤ, or empty String, ToBoolean returns false.
Step 3 of ToBoolean is replaced in B.3.6.1 with a check: if argument is Object and has [[IsHTMLDDA]], return false.
For all remaining values, ToBoolean returns true.
ToBoolean is a pure-returning abstract operation in this clause; no completion/throw result is specified.
The procedure is deterministic for a fixed argument because branch conditions and return values are fixed by that argument.
No explicit exceptional, undefined-behavior, or implementation-defined behavior is stated in the ToBoolean clause or the B.3.6.x replacement text.

Type domain for argument is ECMAScript language value: Undefined, Null, Boolean, String, Symbol, Number, BigInt, Object; this plus default step implies values outside listed falsy/web-compat set return true.
